finding.verdict: two_arm_lift repair is genuinely HIGH-VARIANCE but NOT bimodal all-or-nothing. Across 7 independent campaign runs the held-out validation score spans the full range (0.0, 0.10, 0.80, 0.85, 0.95, 1.0, 1.0). 5/7 runs land a strong program (val >= 0.80); 2/7 land in the weak tail (val <= 0.10). The M3X 0/20 was NOT a fluke or a bug — it is the extreme end of a real, continuous variance distribution, and rep_5 (0.10) independently confirms the weak tail recurs (~2/7 ~= 29% of runs).
finding.mechanism_split: Stage-1 trace-guided repair alone solved 3/5 repeats (rep 1,2,4, all val >= 0.85). Evosearch was the winner in the 2 harder repeats: it rescued rep_3 to a strong 0.80, but on rep_5 it plateaued at dbg 0.667 and the resulting program was weak (0.10). Evosearch reduces but does not eliminate the weak tail.
finding.answers_handoff_question: Which run was representative — pilot (5/5) or M3X (0/20)? ANSWER: neither extreme is 'the truth'. The representative outcome is a strong-but-imperfect program (median val ~0.85); both extremes are tails of one high-variance distribution.
